div.note: K is from B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 42, after Ine but as a new piece, same hand, c. 1125); the heading is in red, and the ‘um’ of ‘morðslihtum’ was cut off in binding. H (Textus Roffensis f. 31b, as the end of Ine, c. 1120); its heading stands not before the text but in the Af–Ine rubric list on f. 11, and the number CXXI should be struck. The Quadripartitus heading is only in its youngest recension, probably not original. Liebermann dates Blaseras c. 930–75.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 388, October 2026 (MS Cons); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.930–75; ?mid 990's (Wormald)”, now “c.930–75 (Liebermann); ?mid-990s (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.930–75 (Liebermann); ?mid-990s (Wormald)”, now “c.930–75 (Liebermann, I p. 388); ?mid-990s (Wormald)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 388; B 388; Q 389; Cons 389; German 389”; 4 rows of Blas)

note.seg: Die Überschrift ist nicht original, aber vielleicht archetyp, da H's Worte beide auch in Q, eines in B, das andere in C stehen
The heading is not original, but perhaps belongs to the archetype, since both of H’s words also appear in Q, one of them in B and the other in C
Zur Latein. Übs. s. o. II As 6, 2¹
On the Latin translation see above II As 6, 2¹

Nicht ‘Mörder’, wie Q Cons und Wilkins, Thorpe, Schmid übs.—Das Kompositum zitiert Toller nur hierher: ‘murder’ (s. d. morðorsliht [‘slaughter’], mansliht). Eine Urk. Ke 848, angeblich Eadwards III., tatsächlich 12. Jhs., hat morðslecht für ‘murdrum-Abgabe’

Not ‘murderers’, as Q, Cons and Wilkins, Thorpe and Schmid translate.—Toller cites the compound only for this passage: ‘murder’ (see under morðorsliht [‘slaughter’], mansliht). A charter Ke 848, purportedly of Eadward III but in fact of the 12th cent., has morðslecht for ‘murdrum payment’
